- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. - update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

r02.

**Premise correction:** This repository (Memos) has **no per-user API rate-limiting middleware** — it isn't registered anywhere, so there are no request limits to report. The question presumes a component that doesn't exist.

What the API middleware chain actually contains, registered in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-138` via `connect.WithInterceptors(...)`, is exactly four Connect/gRPC interceptors:

- `NewMetadataInterceptor()` — converts HTTP headers to gRPC metadata
- `NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces)` — request logging
- `NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces)` — panic recovery
- `NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer)` — authentication/authorization

All four are defined in `server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`; none does rate limiting.

The only request-size guard nearby is `connect.WithReadMaxBytes(maxAPIRequestBytes)` at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:141` — that caps request *body size*, not request *rate*, and it's global rather than per-user.

Supporting evidence that no rate limiter exists:
- The only occurrences of "rate limit" in the Go code are aspirational documentation, not implementation: a "future consideration" comment in `internal/email/doc.go:86` ("Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse") and an example snippet in `internal/email/README.md:291` referencing `golang.org/x/time/rate`.
- `golang.org/x/time` is only an **indirect** dependency (`go.mod:151`), i.e. not imported by any first-party code.
- A repo-wide search for `rate.?limit`, `throttle`, tollbooth, ulule/limiter, etc. turns up no middleware, interceptor, or HTTP handler implementing rate limiting.

So: there is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware and no associated request limits in this codebase.
